title: PID Step Response
creator: Dan McCreary
subject: Control for Robotics
description: Set the gains Kp, Ki and Kd of a toy joint, switch gravity on or off, and watch the plot of its step response with the overshoot, the settling time and the final angle. Then look at five responses and choose the gain change that fixes each one. Used in Chapter 5.

educational.topic: PID control: proportional, integral and derivative gains
learningObjectives: Infer which gain change fixes a given step response (raise Kp, add Kd, add Ki, lower Ki, or no change) in five scenarios, with at least 4 of 5 correct on the first attempt

pedagogical.teachingStrategy: Change one gain at a time and watch the curve, then reason from a symptom on a plotted response to the one term that treats it
keyQuestions: What does Kd do to a joint that overshoots?
Why does gravity leave a gap that Kp alone cannot close?
commonMisconceptions: A higher Kp is always better
The integral term makes the response faster
The derivative term pushes toward the goal
assessmentOpportunities: Five committed choices, one attempt each; 4 of 5 for mastery

controls.label: Raise Kp / Add Kd / Add Ki / Lower Ki / No change
